slides.title: Evidence Gaps as a Planning Pillar
bullets: An earlier module covered what an evidence gap is and how to identify one
This lesson covers how gaps formally integrate into the Medical Plan
They become a core decision pillar, not a loose list of field observations

slides.title: A Living Inventory, Not an Annual Snapshot
bullets: The gap inventory is the honest picture of what current evidence doesn't answer
Built from systematic literature review, guideline analysis, and MSL insights
It must stay live and updated across the whole plan cycle
Not compiled once a year and archived

slides.title: Prioritization Criteria for Evidence Gaps
bullets: Clinical impact: how many patients are affected, and how severely
Feasibility of generating resolving evidence within a reasonable timeframe
Alignment with the strategic imperatives defined for this cycle
Competitive or reputational risk of leaving the gap unaddressed

slides.title: Every Prioritized Gap Becomes a Concrete Initiative
bullets: A subpopulation gap can become an observational or RWE study proposal
A head-to-head comparison gap can prioritize a pragmatic study
A mechanism-of-action understanding gap can become a medical education priority
This explicit link gives the whole Medical Plan its internal coherence

slides.title: From Anecdotal Insight to Strategic Contribution
bullets: Participate in the full process, not just in submitting individual insights
Understand how gaps are aggregated, prioritized, and turned into decisions
This lets you explain to a KOL exactly where an unanswered question stands

takeaway.title: Evidence gaps become a Medical Plan pillar only once prioritized and actioned
bullets: A gap inventory must be kept alive and current, not built once a year
Clear criteria decide which gaps get resources this cycle
Each prioritized gap maps to a specific initiative elsewhere in the plan
